key_insight: A training-free diagnostic framework uses medical ontology and symbolic-probabilistic knowledge graphs to map patient observations to candidate diseases without learning from outcome labels.
clinical_relevance: The approach aims to make clinical reasoning more explicit, auditable, and coverage-aware, with missing-versus-unavailable evidence handled separately.
method: Builds candidate-specific Evidence Feature Nodes from patient-reference matching.
Uses a bounded Information Gate and knowledge-weighted evidence accumulation with disease similarity and clinical rules.
Separates label-free K-means cohort clustering from diagnosis scoring using derived evidence coordinates, not raw predictors or targets.
evidence_signal: Across six retrospective cohorts, the label-free protocol reported high and variable performance, including positive-class F1 scores from 0.634 to 0.996 and full partition-decision coverage.
watch_item: Because evaluation is retrospective and one cohort includes confirmatory PCR rather than true pre-test prediction, prospective clinical validity and generalizability remain unproven.
paper_title: Training-Free Clinical Reasoning through Medical Ontologies and Cognitive Mapping: A Symbolic-Probabilistic Knowledge Graph Framework
